research_question: To evaluate the long-term availability and quality of water resources in generally undeveloped basins at Fort Irwin National Training Center, California, by characterizing aquifer properties, groundwater levels, gradients, and water quality using hydrologic testing and data analysis.

phase_1.user_prompt: I am investigating groundwater contamination, recharge sources, and groundwater age in desert basins. I need to find the USGS parameter codes for discrete water-quality samples of dissolved (filtered) Arsenic in micrograms per liter, dissolved (filtered) Fluoride in milligrams per liter, unfiltered stable isotopes delta Oxygen-18 and delta Deuterium in per mil, and filtered Carbon-14 in percent modern carbon.

phase_3.user_prompt: Process the retrieved water-quality data to isolate the samples for filtered Arsenic. Find the maximum concentration of Arsenic recorded among all the specified wells during this time period. Report the result in milligrams per liter (mg/L).

phase_4.user_prompt: First, what is the minimum Carbon-14 activity (in percent modern carbon) recorded among these sites during the specified period? Second, create a scatter plot of delta Oxygen-18 (x-axis) versus delta Deuterium (y-axis) for the retrieved samples. Save the plot as `fort_irwin_isotopes_plot.png`. Based on the distribution of the isotopic data and the Carbon-14 results, what can be inferred about the recharge history of the groundwater, and which specific wells or groups of wells show the strongest evidence of evaporation prior to recharge?

checkpoint.reference_conclusion: The extremely low Carbon-14 activities (ranging down to ~7.87 pmc) indicate that the groundwater is very old and recharged thousands of years ago. The isotope plot shows that most samples fall below the Global Meteoric Water Line, indicating evaporation prior to recharge. The most enriched (heaviest) isotopic signatures falling along a distinct evaporative trend line correspond to the CRTH1, CRTH2, and LL04 wells.
checkpoint.visual_description: A scatter plot with delta Oxygen-18 on the x-axis (ranging from roughly -14 to -10 per mil) and delta Deuterium on the y-axis (ranging from roughly -105 to -85 per mil). The points should form a positive linear trend typical of an evaporative trend line, falling below the typical slope of 8 for the Global Meteoric Water Line.
